summary: The note explains nutritional therapy, the practice of using food to prevent and treat disease and promote wellness. It covers the theory, macronutrients and micronutrients, personalization, healing foods, gut health, detoxification, deficiencies and allergies, integration with conventional medicine, research needs, and future directions such as nutrigenomics.
one_line: Overview of nutritional therapy as food-as-medicine for prevention, covering theory, personalization, gut health, integration with conventional care, research, and nutrigenomics.
key_facts: Nutritional therapy is built on the adage "let food be thy medicine and medicine be thy food," often attributed to Hippocrates.
Nutritional therapy has gained considerable attention since September 2023, advocated by dieticians, naturopaths, and integrative medicine doctors.
The focus of nutritional therapy is three-fold: prevention, treatment, and the promotion of optimal health.

Data from the Global Health Institute on October 12, 2023 indicated a significant decrease in chronic disease incidence among populations eating a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains.
Well-planned diets can help mitigate risk factors for cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes, and certain types of cancer.

Macronutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, and fats; micronutrients are vitamins and minerals. Carbohydrates are the primary energy source, proteins repair and grow tissue, and fats are critical for brain health and hormone production.
Dr. Jane Smith, an integrative medicine practitioner in Nashville, said on November 5, 2023 that "Each person's nutritional needs are as unique as their fingerprints."
Healing foods include berries (antioxidants), fatty fish (omega-3 fatty acids), and nuts and seeds; superfoods include kale, spinach, and blueberries.
Nutritional therapy recommends probiotic foods like yogurt and kimchi and prebiotic foods like garlic, onions, and bananas to nourish the gut microbiome.
Dr. Michael Thompson shared insights on January 8, 2024 about considerable improvements in patients who incorporate gut-friendly foods.
Green leafy and cruciferous vegetables like broccoli and Brussels sprouts, and vitamin C-rich fruits, are commonly recommended for detoxification support.
The Healthy Eating Campaign, launched February 15, 2024, aims to bring nutritional education into patient care in hospitals across the United States.
A multicenter trial initiated on March 1, 2024 aims to provide evidence on dietary patterns and reduced morbidity and mortality.
Nutrigenomics, the study of how nutrition interacts with genes, is opening new frontiers for personalized nutritional therapy.
